# Draft:5th General Assembly of Prince Edward Island

}}
The 5th General Assembly of the Island of St. John represented the colony of Prince Edward Island, then known as St. John's Island, between 1787 and 1790.
The Assembly sat at the pleasure of the Governor of St. John's Island, Edmund Fanning (colonial administrator).
In September 1787, the colony's first newspaper, The Royal American Gazette and Weekly Intelligencer of the Island of Saint John, began publication in Charlottetown. It played a crucial role in documenting the proceedings of the House of Assembly and local political debates, including issues surrounding Loyalist land claims.
Phillips Callbeck was chosen as speaker.
